author: historian-agent:mig-1
title: First peopling of Sahul (Australia and New Guinea)
summary: Modern humans crossed island Southeast Asia and the sea gaps of Wallacea to reach Sahul, the joined Australia and New Guinea landmass. A 2017 study of Madjedbebe claims about 65,000 years ago; other researchers argue for about 50,000 years. Dated sites from Borneo to New Ireland show the spread through the north.

uncertainty.note: Years are 1950 minus the age. Start: the Madjedbebe luminescence date of about 65,000 years ago (University of Queensland 2017); O'Connell et al. 2018 give 52.7-65.0 ka for the Madjedbebe phase and argue colonisation was about 50 ka, calling the older dates unlikely. The route here uses dated sites that are not in dispute in order: Niah 48-50 ka, Ivane Valley 49-44 ka, Buang Merabak 44 ka. Madjedbebe, Nauwalabila and Australian sites are not waypoints because their dates are the debated ones.

as_recorded.value: Aboriginal people have been in Australia for at least 65,000 years (Madjedbebe)
Madjedbebe Phase 2 range 52.7-65.0 ka; authors reject ages above 50 ka and favour about 50 ka for Sahul
Archaeological AMH remains at Niah by 48-50 ka
Ivane Valley campsites occupied 44-49,000 years ago

when.display: c. 65,000 or c. 50,000 to 44,000 years ago (arrival date debated)

where.modern_name: Niah Caves, Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo (first waypoint; national park centroid)
where.historical_name: Pleistocene Sundaland, the exposed Southeast Asian shelf; no polities or place names exist at this date

waypoints.date: Archaeological AMH remains by 48-50 ka (O'Connell et al. 2018)
waypoints.label: Niah Cave, Borneo (Sunda): human remains by 48-50 ka, with the Niah skull itself at about 40 ka. Point is the national park centroid.

Ivane Valley, Owen Stanley Range, Papua New Guinea (about 2,000 m altitude): campsites 49,000-44,000 years old. Point is Kokoda town, the nearest named place in the source; the site coordinates are not published there.
Buang Merabak, New Ireland, Bismarck Archipelago: occupation dated 44 ka, an island reached by sea.

importance.justification: The earliest sea-crossing colonisation of a new continent and the origin of Aboriginal Australian and Papuan lineages.

related.because: Groups from the out-of-Africa population spread east across Southeast Asia to Sahul.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the route does not reach Australia, because dated Australian sites (Madjedbebe 65 ka claim; Warratyi 49 ka and others, not opened) would break the date order of a single path; Ivane Valley coordinates are a proxy (Kokoda); Niah is a park centroid. 65 versus 50 ka debate is stated in when and summary.

beats.caption: Modern human remains are present at Niah Cave in Borneo by 48,000-50,000 years ago, at the edge of the Sunda shelf.
People camp in the New Guinea highlands at Ivane Valley about 2,000 metres up, 44,000-49,000 years ago.
By 44,000 years ago people occupy New Ireland, an island reached only by sea, showing deliberate crossings. Claims of 65,000 years remain disputed.
